This Agenda contains a brief general description of each item to be considered. Copies of the Staff reports or

  agenda items may call the City Manager at (310) 603-0220, ext. 200.

  Procedures for Addressing the Council

  IN ORDER TO EXPEDITE CITY COUNCIL BUSINESS, WE ASK THAT ALL PERSONS WISHING TO ADDRESS THE
  COUNCIL SUBMIT YOUR COMMENTS IN ADVANCE TO CITYCLERK@LYNWOOD.CA.US OR FILL OUT A FORM
  PROVIDED AT THE PODIUM, AND TO TURN IT IN TO THE CITY CLERK PRIOR TO THE START OF THE
  MEETING. FAILURE TO FILL OUT SUCH A FORM WILL PROHIBIT YOU FROM ADDRESSING THE COUNCIL IN
  THE ABSENCE OF THE UNANIMOUS CONSENT OF THE COUNCIL.

  12.  ADVERTISEMENT OF VACANT CITY TREASURER SEAT
  Comments:
  The City Treasurer position has become vacant with the election of Gabriela Camacho to City
  Council. Under Government Code Section 36512(b), the City must either appoint a person or call
  for a special election to fill the vacancy.

  The vacancy commences when the City Treasurer takes oath of office as a Council Member.
  However, if the City Council does not appoint a replacement by the 60-day deadline, then it must
  call a special election to fill the vacancy. (government Code Section 1770, 36512) (CM)

  Recommendation:
  It is recommended that the City Council of the City of Lynwood open the application process for
  30 days and appoint a resident to fill the vacant City Treasurer seat.

  AND SUCH OTHER MATTERS AS ARE PROVIDED BY LAW

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council take the following actions:

  1. Adopt the attached resolution entitled "A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  LYNWOOD, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA, RECITING THE FACT OF
  THE GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION HELD OF NOVEMBER 8, 2022, DECLARING THE
  RESULT AND SUCH OTHER MATTERS AS ARE PROVIDED BY LAW"; and
  2. Receive and file Exhibit "A", Certificate of Canvass and Statement of Votes Cast as provided by the Los
  Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk.

  Background:

  A General Municipal Election was held in the City of Lynwood on Tuesday November 8, 2022. California
  Elections Code Section 10263 states upon the completion of the official canvass of results by the County, prior to
  the installation of new officers, the City Council shall adopt a resolution reciting the facts of the election and
  declaring elected the persons for whom the highest number of votes were case for each office

  Discussion and Analysis:

  As a result of said election, the Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk has canvassed the returns
  and certified the results as reflected in the attached resolution. Attached to the resolution is Exhibit "A", which will
  be updated upon receipt of the official ballot count by the Los Angeles County Registrar Recorder's Office on

  SUBJECT:  CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council make appointments to Mayor and Mayor Pro-Tem.

  Background:

  Traditionally the City Council reorganizes by nominating and appointing one of its members to serve as Mayor or
  Mayor Pro-Tem. This process is consistent with Government Code Section 36801, which states, "The City
  Council shall meet at the meeting at which the declaration of the election results for the General Municipal Election
  is made pursuant to Sections 10262 and 10263 of the Elections Code and following the declaration of the election
  results and the installation of elected officials, choose one of its members as Mayor, and one of its members as
  Mayor Pro Tempore."

  Ordinance First Reading  ORDINANCE NO. 1748

  John Yonai, Interim Director of Community Development provided a power point
  presentation via Zoom along with Senior Planner Alfredo Perez joining at the Council
  Chamber podium. He also invited the proponent Mark Kudler to address a number of
  items which may impact the ordinance and therefore he requested to have revisions read
  into the record. Interim Director Yonai noted that the first item for Council consideration
  this evening is 11104 and 11106 Wright Road which is one of the locations that the
  proponent Bulletin Board Displays and Mark Kudler have proposed and been working for
  the past eighteen (18) months which included his involvement in the project beginning in
  November. He stated that the site plan proposed to allow for an 80-foot tall back-to-back
  digital billboard and he wants to correct that read as a possible V-shaped back-to-back
  digital billboard that provides more angular viewing to the freeway and actually sheds light
  away from potential residential impacts and indicated that the proposed billboard total sign
  area is approximately 14’ X 48’ or 1,350 square feet. He additionally remarked that the
  proposed 80 feet is measured from the apex of the adjacent freeway to the top of the 14-
  foot sign face and that the applicant is proposing an additional seven (7) feet of height to
  accommodate the proposed sign’s artwork beyond the sign display. If approved, the sign
  height will exceed 80 feet in height.

  MOTION: It was moved by Mayor Pro Tem Solache, seconded by Council Member Soto
  to approve staff’s recommendations. Motion carried by 5-0 vote

  SUBJECT:  ADVERTISEMENT OF VACANT CITY TREASURER SEAT

  Recommendation:

  It is recommended that the City Council of the City of Lynwood open the application process for 30 days and
  appoint a resident to fill the vacant City Treasurer seat.

  Background:

  The City Treasurer position has become vacant with the election of Gabriela Camacho to the City Council. Under
  Government Code Section 36512(b), the City must either appoint a person or call for a special election to fill the
  vacancy:

  "If a vacancy occurs in an elective office provided for in this chapter, the council shall, within 60 days from the
  commencement of the vacancy, either fill the vacancy by appointment or call a special election to fill the vacancy. The
  special election shall be held on the next regularly established election not less than 114 days from the call of the special
  election. A person appointed or elected to fill a vacancy holds office for the unexpired term of the former incumbent."

  The vacancy commences when the City Treasurer takes the oath of office as a Council Member. However, if the
  City Council does not appoint a replacement by the 60-day deadline, then it must call a special election to fill the
  vacancy. (Government Code Section 1770, 36512).

  Discussion and Analysis:

  The Lynwood Municipal Code does not lay out an appointment process for filling vacancies in elective offices. However,
  state law places some limitations on the appointment process. Government Code Section 36502(a) states:

  "A person is not eligible to hold office as councilmember, city clerk, or city treasurer
  unless he or she is at the time of assuming the office an elector of the city, and was a
  registered voter of the city at the time nomination papers are issued to the candidate
  as provided for in Section 10227 of the Election Code.

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 45 of 46
   "If, during his or her term of office, he or she moves his or her place of residence outside
  of the city limits or ceases to be an elector of the city, his or her office shall immediately
  become vacant."
  Any appointee to the City Treasurer position must be a Lynwood resident and registered to vote
  in Lynwood. In addition, the Brown Act requires any interviews be conducted by the entire City
  Council in open session.
  Incompatibility of Offices:
  It would not be an incompatibility of office of conflict for an employee in Lynwood to also serve as City
  Treasurer. It is done in a large number of cities throughout the State of California. An incompatibility of
  office issue arises if a current staff position can be characterized as an "officer' position. An
  individualized analysis of the employee's job description and classification is required to determine
  whether the employee may be classified as an "officer".

  Other available options:
  1. Call for a Special Election. Staff can reach out to the County to get an estimate on the
  cost for the special election.
  2. Appoint a Resident to be City Treasurer. City Council could direct that the position be
  advertised for 30 days. Applicants could be required to submit a letter of interest, resume,
  City application and references. City Council could then conduct public interviews and
  make a selection.
  3. Appoint an Employee to be City Treasurer to Fill the Unexpired
  Term (Two Years) of Elected City Treasurer. Under this option the City Treasurer's functions
  would be consolidated in the Finance Department as is the case in a large number of California
  cities. An employee, who is a resident of the City, would be appointed City Treasurer to fill the
  unexpired term of the City Treasurer. This option would provide supervision, management
  oversight and accountability. The Finance Department estimates the cost savings to be
  approximately $18,000 per year plus a portion of the department operating costs.
  4. Do Option #2 and Option #3 Toqether. Under this option the City Council could begin
  advertising for a resident to fill the position while continuing to consider appointing an
  employee to fill the unexpired term of the elected treasurer. The City Council would then
  decide before the end of the 60-day statutory limit whether to appoint an employee or a
  resident to the position.
  It is recommended that the City Council appoint a resident to fill the vacant City Treasurer seat
  and direct staff to advertise the vacancy for 30 days. Applicants would be required to submit a
  letter of interest, resume, City application and references. City Council could then conduct public
  interviews and make a selection at a future meeting that would be held within the 60-day
  appointment period.

  Fiscal Impact:

  There is no fiscal impact with making an appointment to the City Treasurer vacancy.
